Update:

Hello,

you are of course absolutely right. Bonobos are equally distant to people from Africa, Europe or anywhere else in the world.

The X/A ratio measures something completely different: It compares individuals from a certain group (bonobos, chimpanzees, or human populations) and compares how different the X autosomes in this group are from the autosomes (the non-sex-chromosomes, i.e. everything that is not X and Y). Since each generation you have three X chromosomes per four autosomes (XX for the mother + XY from the dad = three X), you would expect that the ratio should be 3/4 (thats why there is a dashed line at 0.75 in the plot). But there are many ways in which this measure could be nudged off this expected value. That Europeans look different in this measure could for instance be explained by later waves of primarily male migrants out of Africa that mixed with people in Europe, but there are other ideas as well.

little vocab first * Distro: A custom combination of software bundled with the linux kernel * LiveUSB: This is a distros install media, that can also be ran as the full OS, albiet it won't save any files unless you do some advaned set up. Imagine it like recovery media, or install media, that is also the full OS at the same time. * Package Manager: basically like an App Store (with way less restrictions than anything apple or microsoft has, and a much greater selection) It handles updating the OS, applications, removing them, removing their config files, managing dependancies, etc. If the software runs on linux, and is licensed sanely (like most linux software), its going to be in there (unless its really new). One of the reasons you don't have to worry about viruses on linux (another because the robustness and modularity), as pretty much no linux user downloads software from the internet. They can get all their software offical vetted.

Well there is multiple ways to go through this. you can duel boot which installs both OSes side by side. You could also copy her whole user folder to external media.

The best way to do it would be to get some external drive. (The 1TB ones at bestbuy are pretty cheap). Once you've booted into the live LinuxUSB, you just erase all the factory set partitions on the external drive, using gparted and then copy every partition over from the laptop into the external drive (still using gparted). This will make an exact copy, OS, personal files, and all. If you wanted to you could then copy all thsoe partitions back over, and it would be just like it was, nothing out of place. You can then sort through the personal files at your leasure as you can acess it like any flashdrive or external media.

gparted should be on installed on the liveUSB by default, but its not too hard to install from the package manager.

Its recommended to do this because: A) you have everything backuped and disconnected, and thus can wipe windows 10 with out fear. Since duelbooting has both OSes installed side by side, and you boot into one of them at boot up, the OS is not running, and thus you could accidently screw it up if you don't know what you're doing.

(However this is mostly about windows, because windows is infamouse for being known to be a bitch to other OSes, like installing over them, not detecting partitions as valid, over writting bootloaders, refusing to be partition a certain way. Would not trust windows10 auto updates with that)
